nuggets.text: Joe Moglia, a Fordham alum who coached Coastal Carolina from 2012 to 2018, is the man the Rams' Moglia Stadium is named for.
The Rams played in the first televised college football game ever, against Waynesburg in 1939.
The Rams are credited with inspiring the term Ivy League, after a sportswriter compared them to Princeton and Yale.
The Cleveland club that became the Los Angeles Rams took the name Rams in honor of Fordham.
Vince Lombardi was one of Fordham's famed Seven Blocks of Granite, the Rams' rock-solid line of the 1930s.
Rams coach Joe Conlin won Ivy League titles as an assistant at both Harvard (2011) and Yale (2017).
At the Rams' home in the Bronx, the football field is laid out in the baseball outfield.
The Rams and Chanticleers meet on the football field for the first time ever on Saturday.
The Rams once moved their home games off campus to the 55,000-seat Polo Grounds in upper Manhattan.
Linebacker Andrew Osmun leads the Rams with 23 tackles through two games.
